title: Load testing and capacity model
goal: Prove the system's capacity and find its limits: scripted load tests for the API and the relay (including reconnect storms and multi-node routing), and a capacity model that turns measured per-instance numbers into instance counts and cost for launch targets.
scope_in: k6 scenarios for REST (`infra/loadtest/k6/api-mixed.js`: /v1/me, sessions list, join-token, usage ingest, entitlements) and a Node-based WebSocket load driver built on the client simulator (B011) for the relay (handshake, steady chat traffic with random ciphertext, queue ops, presence, resume).

Launch targets encoded as thresholds: 20 000 concurrent WS connections cluster-wide; 2 000 concurrent sessions of avg 5 members; 5 000 sequenced frames/s aggregate; fan-out p95 < 150 ms and p99 < 400 ms in-region; API 500 req/s mixed with p95 < 300 ms and p99 < 800 ms and error rate < 0.5 %; usage ingest 100 batches/s.

Scenarios: ramp (0 -> target in 10 min), soak (1 h at 70 % target), spike (x2 for 2 min), reconnect storm (kill one relay node holding 5 000 connections, all clients resumed within 60 s with no seq gap), cross-node fan-out (members of one session spread over 3 nodes).

Capacity model script `infra/loadtest/capacity/model.ts`: inputs are measured connections/instance at CPU 60 %, memory per connection, frames/s per vCPU, API req/s per instance; outputs instance counts for 1x, 2x, 5x launch targets with N+1, plus monthly cost estimate from a price table.
Result artefacts: `infra/loadtest/reports/<date>-<scenario>.json` (k6 summary + resource samples) and `docs/ops/capacity-model.md` generated from the latest report.
Safety: synthetic data only, tests run against stage; refusal to run against prod hostnames.
scope_out: Building dashboards (B093) or tuning relay code (findings are filed against the owning lanes).
build_against: Run scaled-down profiles (200 connections, 20 req/s) against the compose stack from B012 with the simulator from B011 and the real relay cross-node routing; full-scale runs occur against stage by the owner. No real client is needed.
interfaces: Commands: `pnpm loadtest:api --profile smoke|ramp|soak|spike`, `pnpm loadtest:relay --profile smoke|ramp|soak|storm|crossnode`, `pnpm capacity:model --report <file>`.
Env: `LOADTEST_TARGET` (must match allow-list `*.stage.centcom.dev` or `localhost`), `LOADTEST_TOKEN_MINT_URL` (stage test-only minter).
Report JSON `{scenario, started_at, target, thresholds: [{name, ok, value, limit}], resources: {...}, passed: boolean}`.
k6 thresholds as code in each scenario file; capacity model exports `plan(targets, measurements): InstancePlan`.
acceptance: The `smoke` profile (200 connections, 20 req/s, 3 min) runs in CI-sized time (< 5 min) against the compose stack and passes thresholds; thresholds are assertions (non-zero exit on breach).

In stage, the `ramp` profile reaches 20 000 connections and 5 000 frames/s and the report shows fan-out p95 < 150 ms, p99 < 400 ms, close code 4429/4503 rate < 0.1 %, no frame loss (every sequenced frame delivered to all session members, verified by seq continuity checks in the driver).
The `storm` profile kills one relay node holding 5 000 connections: >= 99.9 % of clients resume (via hot buffer or snapshot path) within 60 s, with no duplicate or missing seq after dedupe.
The API mix at 500 req/s for 30 min has p95 < 300 ms, p99 < 800 ms, error rate < 0.5 %, and 429 responses appear only on deliberately over-limit buckets.
`pnpm capacity:model` produces a table with instance counts for 1x/2x/5x targets with N+1 headroom and cost, and fails when any input measurement is older than 30 days.
The runner refuses to start when `LOADTEST_TARGET` is not allow-listed (test with `api.centcom.dev` -> exit code 2).
All frames sent by the driver carry random bytes in `ct`; a scan of the relay logs and DB after a run finds none of the driver's canary strings.
tests: unit tests for the capacity model (known inputs -> known outputs), threshold evaluation and target allow-list.
smoke profile in CI nightly against compose.
driver self-test: seq continuity checker detects injected gaps and duplicates.
dry-run test of the prod refusal.
guardrails: MUST NOT run against production hostnames or production credentials; the allow-list check is in code and in the workflow.
MUST use synthetic users/workspaces created with a test-only minter that exists only in stage/dev.
MUST NOT send real content: ciphertext is random bytes; no real emails or personal data in fixtures.
MUST cap the load generator's own resources (connections per process <= 5 000) and document the number of generator hosts needed.
MUST clean up created sessions/users after runs (`pnpm loadtest:cleanup`).
failure_modes: Generator saturation (CPU > 85 %) -> run marked invalid, not passed, to avoid false results.
Stage throttled by Fly or provider limits -> run aborts with explicit reason and partial report.
Token minter unavailable -> run aborts before generating load.
notes: SPLIT? L-size is realistic only if the WS driver reuses the simulator; if B011 lacks bulk-client support, a thin driver is built here. Launch numbers (20k connections etc.) are working assumptions to be ratified by product; changing them only changes thresholds. A stage-only token minter is a test hook and must be provided by the auth lanes behind a stage-only flag; if missing, the driver uses the device flow with pre-seeded users.
